Explanation of the words:

Ḥā Mīm: This is one of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿah), written thus: Ḥā Mīm, and read: Ḥā Mīm.

Tanzīl al-Kitāb min Allāh: That is, the revelation of the Qur'an is from God.

Al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAlīm: That is, the One who prevails over His purpose, the All-Knowing of His servants, outwardly and inwardly, in their present state and their final outcome.

Ghāfir al-dhanb: That is, the forgiver of the sin of whoever repents to God and returns to His obedience after disobeying Him.

Shadīd al-ʿiqāb dhī al-ṭawl: That is, severe in punishment toward those who disbelieve in Him; dhī al-ṭawl means abundant bounty toward those who believe in Him and obey Him.

Lā ilāha illā Huwa, ilayhi al-maṣīr: That is, there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, and to Him is the return of all creatures.

Mā yujādilu fī āyāt Allāh illā alladhīna kafarū: That is, in the Qur'an, to nullify it, except the disbelievers.

Fa-lā yaghurrannaka taqallubuhum fī al-bilād: That is, do not be deceived by their living in safety, for their final end is the Fire.

Wa al-aḥzāb min baʿdihim: That is, and the factions after them denied, namely the people of ʿĀd, Thamūd, and the people of Lūṭ, after the people of Nūḥ.

Wa hammat kull ummah bi-rasūlihim li-yakhudhūh: That is, to enable them to reach him with whatever torment and killing they intended.

Wa jādalū bi al-bāṭil li-yudḥidū bihi al-ḥaqq: That is, to remove the truth through it and nullify it.

Fa-kayfa kāna ʿiqāb: That is, it befell its proper target, as He destroyed them and left none of them.

Kadhālika ḥaqqat kalimat Rabbika ʿalā alladhīna kafarū: That is, the word of punishment was due upon those who disbelieved.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted: Ḥā Mīm: God knows best what He means by it.

We have mentioned more than once that these letters serve two purposes. The first is that the Arab polytheists of Makkah had forbidden the inhabitants from listening to the Qur'an, lest they be affected by it and abandon their gods. God related of them in Surah Fuṣṣilat, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it that you may overcome."﴾ [41:26]. So these disjointed letters, with their particular melody, would captivate them so that they would listen, and this was a great benefit. The second is that when the polytheists insisted that the Qur'an was not revelation but was of the same kind as the speech of poets, soothsayers, and purveyors of myths, God challenged them to produce its like, and it is composed of these same letters: Alif Lām Mīm, Ṭā Sīn, Ḥā Mīm. What strengthens this view is that the Qur'an is often mentioned right after these letters, such as: Alif Lām Mīm. Those are the verses of the Book (2:1–2); Ḥā Mīm. The revelation of the Book (40:1–2); Ḥā Mīm. By the Clear Book (43:1–2). These two benefits are among the finest things derived by the scholars of Qur'anic exegesis, and beyond them, there is no good in transmitting anything, for it lacks a reasonable benefit, and nothing has been transmitted from the Messenger or his Companions.

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾, He informs that He, mighty and majestic, is the source of this Qur'an, for He sent it down as a revelation to His servant and messenger. He described Himself with might and knowledge, saying "al-ʿAzīz," that is, in His retribution against His enemies, the One who prevails over His command and purpose, so that nothing can come between Him and what He wills; "al-ʿAlīm," the All-Knowing of His creatures, their needs and requirements, so He sent down the Book for their guidance and reform.

As for His saying: ﴿Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, Full of bounty﴾, know that He, may He be exalted, forgives the sins of those who seek forgiveness, accepts the repentance of those who repent, and that He has made punishment severe for those who disbelieve in Him and disobey Him. His saying "dhī al-ṭawl" means abundant favor and great grace. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾, that is, there is no one worthy of worship except Him, the Mighty, the Wise: Mighty, prevailing over His command, Wise in the management of His creation.

When the Blessed and Exalted One praised Himself with what befits Him, He informed His Messenger that ﴿none dispute concerning the signs of God﴾, the Qur'anic verses containing decisive proofs and clear evidences of God's oneness, of meeting Him, and of the prophethood of the Messenger of God, ﴿except those who disbelieve﴾. This is due to the darkness of their souls and the corruption of their hearts. Therefore, be patient and do not be deceived by the outward appearance of their state of abundant provision and bodily health. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So let not their movement throughout the land deceive you﴾, that is, secure and healthy in their bodies and their provisions, for they are given respite, not neglected. The evidence: ﴿Before them the people of Nūḥ denied, and the factions after them﴾, ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Ibrāhīm, the people of Lūṭ, the companions of Madyan, and Pharaoh. Every nation among those nations intended to seize its messenger to kill him or to torment him. They disputed with falsehood, just as your people from Quraysh dispute, in order to remove the truth through it, that is, to eliminate and push it away by their falsehood. Then We seized them; so how was My punishment? That is, it befell its proper target, and praise be to God, for He cut off their root and ended their existence and their opposition.

As for His saying: ﴿And thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved, that they are companions of the Fire﴾, that is, just as His judgment was due to destroy those nations that denied their messengers, and God indeed destroyed them, so the word of your Lord was fulfilled against those who disbelieved, because they are the companions of the Fire. The intended "word of your Lord" is His saying: "I will surely fill Hell," and so on.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing that the Noble Qur'an's source of revelation is God Most High, for He is the One who inspired it and sent it down upon the Messenger Muḥammad (ﷺ), and by this the prophethood of the Messenger Muḥammad (ﷺ) is established.

2- Clarifying the greatness of the Lord, Most High, manifested in His names: al-ʿAzīz, al-ʿAlīm, al-Ḥakīm, dhī al-ṭawl, ghāfir al-dhanb, qābil al-tawb; there is no deity except Him.

3- Establishing monotheism, resurrection, and recompense.

4- Establishing the principle that God gives respite and does not neglect, and that His seizure is severe.

Ḥā Mīm: This is one of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿah), written thus: Ḥā Mīm, and read: Ḥā Mīm.

Tanzīl al-Kitāb min Allāh: That is, the revelation of the Qur'an is from God.

Al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAlīm: That is, the One who prevails over His purpose, the All-Knowing of His servants, outwardly and inwardly, in their present state and their final outcome.

Ghāfir al-dhanb: That is, the forgiver of the sin of whoever repents to God and returns to His obedience after disobeying Him.

Shadīd al-ʿiqāb dhī al-ṭawl: That is, severe in punishment toward those who disbelieve in Him; dhī al-ṭawl means abundant bounty toward those who believe in Him and obey Him.

Lā ilāha illā Huwa, ilayhi al-maṣīr: That is, there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, and to Him is the return of all creatures.

Mā yujādilu fī āyāt Allāh illā alladhīna kafarū: That is, in the Qur'an, to nullify it, except the disbelievers.

Fa-lā yaghurrannaka taqallubuhum fī al-bilād: That is, do not be deceived by their living in safety, for their final end is the Fire.

Wa al-aḥzāb min baʿdihim: That is, and the factions after them denied, namely the people of ʿĀd, Thamūd, and the people of Lūṭ, after the people of Nūḥ.

Wa hammat kull ummah bi-rasūlihim li-yakhudhūh: That is, to enable them to reach him with whatever torment and killing they intended.

Wa jādalū bi al-bāṭil li-yudḥidū bihi al-ḥaqq: That is, to remove the truth through it and nullify it.

Fa-kayfa kāna ʿiqāb: That is, it befell its proper target, as He destroyed them and left none of them.

Kadhālika ḥaqqat kalimat Rabbika ʿalā alladhīna kafarū: That is, the word of punishment was due upon those who disbelieved.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted: Ḥā Mīm: God knows best what He means by it.

We have mentioned more than once that these letters serve two purposes. The first is that the Arab polytheists of Makkah had forbidden the inhabitants from listening to the Qur'an, lest they be affected by it and abandon their gods. God related of them in Surah Fuṣṣilat, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it that you may overcome."﴾ [41:26]. So these disjointed letters, with their particular melody, would captivate them so that they would listen, and this was a great benefit. The second is that when the polytheists insisted that the Qur'an was not revelation but was of the same kind as the speech of poets, soothsayers, and purveyors of myths, God challenged them to produce its like, and it is composed of these same letters: Alif Lām Mīm, Ṭā Sīn, Ḥā Mīm. What strengthens this view is that the Qur'an is often mentioned right after these letters, such as: Alif Lām Mīm. Those are the verses of the Book (2:1–2); Ḥā Mīm. The revelation of the Book (40:1–2); Ḥā Mīm. By the Clear Book (43:1–2). These two benefits are among the finest things derived by the scholars of Qur'anic exegesis, and beyond them, there is no good in transmitting anything, for it lacks a reasonable benefit, and nothing has been transmitted from the Messenger or his Companions.

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾, He informs that He, mighty and majestic, is the source of this Qur'an, for He sent it down as a revelation to His servant and messenger. He described Himself with might and knowledge, saying "al-ʿAzīz," that is, in His retribution against His enemies, the One who prevails over His command and purpose, so that nothing can come between Him and what He wills; "al-ʿAlīm," the All-Knowing of His creatures, their needs and requirements, so He sent down the Book for their guidance and reform.

As for His saying: ﴿Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, Full of bounty﴾, know that He, may He be exalted, forgives the sins of those who seek forgiveness, accepts the repentance of those who repent, and that He has made punishment severe for those who disbelieve in Him and disobey Him. His saying "dhī al-ṭawl" means abundant favor and great grace. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾, that is, there is no one worthy of worship except Him, the Mighty, the Wise: Mighty, prevailing over His command, Wise in the management of His creation.

When the Blessed and Exalted One praised Himself with what befits Him, He informed His Messenger that ﴿none dispute concerning the signs of God﴾, the Qur'anic verses containing decisive proofs and clear evidences of God's oneness, of meeting Him, and of the prophethood of the Messenger of God, ﴿except those who disbelieve﴾. This is due to the darkness of their souls and the corruption of their hearts. Therefore, be patient and do not be deceived by the outward appearance of their state of abundant provision and bodily health. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So let not their movement throughout the land deceive you﴾, that is, secure and healthy in their bodies and their provisions, for they are given respite, not neglected. The evidence: ﴿Before them the people of Nūḥ denied, and the factions after them﴾, ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Ibrāhīm, the people of Lūṭ, the companions of Madyan, and Pharaoh. Every nation among those nations intended to seize its messenger to kill him or to torment him. They disputed with falsehood, just as your people from Quraysh dispute, in order to remove the truth through it, that is, to eliminate and push it away by their falsehood. Then We seized them; so how was My punishment? That is, it befell its proper target, and praise be to God, for He cut off their root and ended their existence and their opposition.

As for His saying: ﴿And thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved, that they are companions of the Fire﴾, that is, just as His judgment was due to destroy those nations that denied their messengers, and God indeed destroyed them, so the word of your Lord was fulfilled against those who disbelieved, because they are the companions of the Fire. The intended "word of your Lord" is His saying: "I will surely fill Hell," and so on.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing that the Noble Qur'an's source of revelation is God Most High, for He is the One who inspired it and sent it down upon the Messenger Muḥammad (ﷺ), and by this the prophethood of the Messenger Muḥammad (ﷺ) is established.

2- Clarifying the greatness of the Lord, Most High, manifested in His names: al-ʿAzīz, al-ʿAlīm, al-Ḥakīm, dhī al-ṭawl, ghāfir al-dhanb, qābil al-tawb; there is no deity except Him.

3- Establishing monotheism, resurrection, and recompense.

4- Establishing the principle that God gives respite and does not neglect, and that His seizure is severe.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 40, verses 7–9**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"Those who bear the Throne"*: that is, the angels who carry the Throne.

*"And those around it"*: that is, the angels who surround the Throne on all its sides.

*"Glorify their Lord with His praise"*: that is, they say, "Glory be to Allah, and with His praise; Glory be to Allah the Mighty." This is their prayer and their glorification.

*"And believe in Him"*: How could they not, when they are in His presence? But this is a description of their perfection.

*"And ask forgiveness for those who believe"*: that is, they seek forgiveness for the believers, because of the bond of faith in Allah that connects them to them.

*"Our Lord, You have encompassed everything in mercy and knowledge"*: that is, they say, "O our Lord, You have encompassed everything in mercy and knowledge."

*"So forgive those who repent and follow Your way"*: that is, since Your mercy and knowledge encompass all Your creatures, forgive those who turn to You in repentance, worship You, affirm Your oneness, and follow Your way, which is Islam.

*"And protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire"*: that is, keep them safe from the Fire so that You do not punish them with it.

*"Gardens of Eden"*: that is, gardens containing palaces and rivers, for everlasting dwelling.

*"Which You have promised them"*: that is, by His words, Exalted is He: "Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow."

*"And whoever is righteous among their fathers"*: that is, whoever is righteous through faith and was not corrupted by polytheism and disbelief.

*"And protect them from evil deeds"*: that is, keep them safe from the consequence of the evil deeds they committed, so that You do not hold them to account for them.

*"And whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day"*: that is, whoever You protect from the consequence of his evil deeds on the Day of Resurrection, so that You do not call him to account.

*"Then You have had mercy on him"*: that is, by covering him, not exposing him, pardoning him, and not punishing him.

*"That is the great triumph"*: that is, being protected from punishment and being admitted into Paradise is the great triumph.

**The meanings of the verses:**

Allah, Exalted is He, informs us of His greatness and of what necessitates faith in Him, in His signs, in His oneness, and in meeting Him. He says: *"Those who bear the Throne,"* that is, His Throne, from among the angels, *"and those around it"*, the angels who surround His Throne entirely. *"They glorify their Lord with His praise,"* glorifying Him while joining praise to it, by saying, "Glory be to Allah and with His praise." *"And they believe in Him,"* that is, they believe in His oneness and in not associating anyone in His worship. *"And they ask forgiveness for those who believe"*, because of the bond of faith that binds them to them. Perhaps the reason for mentioning their own faith is that the believers are brothers, and their seeking forgiveness is a request to Allah to forgive the believers among His servants. This is the meaning of His words: *"Our Lord, You have encompassed everything in mercy and knowledge."* That is, they say, seeking the means to Him, Glorified and Exalted, through His attributes: *"Our Lord, You have encompassed everything in mercy and knowledge,"* meaning, "O our Lord, Your mercy and knowledge encompass all creatures. So forgive those who repent," that is, turn to You, *"so they abandon polytheism and follow Your way, which is Islam, submitting to Your command and prohibition."* *"And protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire,"* that is, keep them safe, O our Lord, from the punishment of the Fire, and admit them into *"Gardens of Eden,"* that is, a dwelling from which whoever enters does not leave and does not desire to depart, because of the completeness of its bliss and the abundance of happiness in it. *"And whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants,"* that is, also admit whoever is righteous through faith and monotheism among their fathers, spouses, and descendants, and join them to their ranks, so that they may be with them even if their own deeds fall short. Their saying, *"Indeed You, You are the Mighty, the Wise,"* is also a means of seeking His nearness through the attributes of might, dominance, and power over all creatures, and the wisdom manifest in all beings.

Their saying: *"And protect them from evil deeds,"* that is, keep them safe from the consequence of their evil deeds by forgiving them and covering them, so that they become worthy of joining their children, whom we ask You to join with them. *"And whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day,"* that is, the Day of Resurrection, *"then You have had mercy on him."* *"And that is the great triumph,"* that is, deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise is the great triumph, according to His words: *"Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed"* [Aal 'Imran: 185]. The meaning of *"whoever You protect from evil deeds"* is that You protect him from their punishment, by forgiving them and pardoning them, so He does not hold them to account for them. Thus they are saved from the Fire and enter Paradise, and that deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise is the great triumph.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Explanation of the greatness of the Lord, Exalted is He.
2. Explanation of the virtue of faith and its people.
3. The virtue of glorifying Allah by saying, "Glory be to Allah and with His praise." It is authentically related that whoever says it one hundred times in the morning or in the evening, his sins will be forgiven, even if they are like the foam of the sea, meaning in abundance.
4. Good news to the believers that Allah, Exalted is He, will gather them with their fathers, spouses, and descendants in Paradise. Allah has responded to the angels' supplication, and Allah, Exalted is He, has informed us of this in His words: *"And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join their descendants with them"* [At-Tur: 21].

Their saying: *"And protect them from evil deeds,"* that is, keep them safe from the consequence of their evil deeds by forgiving them and covering them, so that they become worthy of joining their children, whom we ask You to join with them. *"And whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day,"* that is, the Day of Resurrection, *"then You have had mercy on him."* *"And that is the great triumph,"* that is, deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise is the great triumph, according to His words: *"Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed"* [Aal 'Imran: 185]. The meaning of *"whoever You protect from evil deeds"* is that You protect him from their punishment, by forgiving them and pardoning them, so He does not hold them to account for them. Thus they are saved from the Fire and enter Paradise, and that deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise is the great triumph.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Explanation of the greatness of the Lord, Exalted is He.
2. Explanation of the virtue of faith and its people.
3. The virtue of glorifying Allah by saying, "Glory be to Allah and with His praise." It is authentically related that whoever says it one hundred times in the morning or in the evening, his sins will be forgiven, even if they are like the foam of the sea, meaning in abundance.
4. Good news to the believers that Allah, Exalted is He, will gather them with their fathers, spouses, and descendants in Paradise. Allah has responded to the angels' supplication, and Allah, Exalted is He, has informed us of this in His words: *"And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join their descendants with them"* [At-Tur: 21].

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 40, verses 10–17:

Explanation of the words:

﴿ينادون لمقت الله﴾: meaning, the angels call out to them, saying: "God's hatred of you is greater than your hatred of yourselves," and maqt (hatred) is the most intense form of dislike.

﴿إذ تدعون إلى الإيمان فتكفرون﴾: meaning, God's hatred of you when you were in the world and were being called to faith but disbelieved is greater than your hatred of yourselves today, when you have seen the punishment.

﴿أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين﴾: meaning, You caused us to die twice: the first time when we were nonexistent and You created us, and the second time when You caused us to die in the world by taking our souls. And You gave us life twice: the first time when You brought us out of our mothers' wombs alive, and this is one life; and the second time after You raised us from our graves alive.

﴿فاعترفنا بذنوبنا﴾: meaning, our sins, which are denying Your signs and the meeting with You, and associating others with You.

﴿فهل إلى خروج من سبيل﴾: meaning, is there any way back to the life of the world a second time, so that we may believe in You, affirm Your oneness, obey You, and not disobey You?

﴿ذلكم﴾: meaning, the punishment you are in.

﴿بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم﴾: meaning, because when God alone was called upon, you disbelieved in His oneness.

﴿يريكم آياته﴾: meaning, the proofs of His oneness and His power to resurrect you and to recompense you.

﴿وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب﴾: meaning, none takes heed except the one who turns back to God and returns to Him in His oneness.

﴿يلقي الروح من أمره﴾: meaning, He casts revelation by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants.

﴿لينذر يوم التلاق﴾: meaning, so that He may warn, through the one to whom revelation is sent from among mankind, who is the Messenger, of the Day when the people of heaven and the people of earth meet, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿يوم هم بارزون﴾: meaning, nothing shields them, neither mountain, nor tree, nor stone.

﴿لمن الملك اليوم﴾: meaning, to whom belongs the sovereignty today.

Meaning of the verses:

After He mentioned the condition of the believers, that they and their spouses and offspring are in the abode of bliss, in these three verses He describes the condition of the disbelievers in the Fire, following the Qur'an's method of encouragement and warning. He, the Exalted, said, reporting about the people of the Fire: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved﴾, meaning, in their Lord, in meeting Him, and in His oneness, ﴿will be called out to﴾, meaning, the angels will call out to them, saying to them, after they begin to loathe themselves and curse one another: ﴿"The hatred of God is greater than your hatred of yourselves"﴾, because you used to be called to faith in God, His oneness, and obedience, but you disbelieved and rejected it out of arrogance.

Here, in the second verse [11], they will say while in Hell: ﴿"Our Lord"﴾, meaning, O our Lord, ﴿"You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice"﴾. By the two deaths they mean: the first, when they were lifeless drops of semen, and the second, the taking of their souls at the end of their terms. By the two lives they mean: the first, which they had in the world before their death, and the second, which is after the resurrection. Their saying ﴿"So we have acknowledged our sins"﴾ means the sins they committed in the worldly life, which are disbelief, polytheism, and disobedience. Their saying after this confession, ﴿"Is there any way out?"﴾, means: is there any path to leave the Fire and return to the worldly life so that we may correct what we corrupted and obey Him whom we disobeyed? The answer is definitely: there is no way to that at all, and your remaining in the punishment is not an injustice to you, but a just recompense for you. Then He mentioned the cause of their punishment in His saying: ﴿"That is because when God alone was called upon, you disbelieved"﴾ in God and His oneness, ﴿"but when partners were associated with Him, you believed"﴾, meaning, when God was associated with others you believed, like your saying "Here I am, no partner have You, except a partner who belongs to You, You possess him and what he possesses," and His saying, "So judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Great." He has decreed your punishment, so there is no path to your salvation.

"So loathe yourselves and lament over your souls; this will neither benefit you nor lighten the punishment for you." His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"It is He who shows you His signs"﴾ is an address to people in this worldly life, an address to the polytheists of Quraysh. After He presented to them a true, living picture of their condition in Hell on the Day of Resurrection, He returned to address them, calling them to faith. He said: He, that is the God who is truly worthy of worship, ﴿who shows you His signs﴾, meaning His proofs and the signs of His oneness and His power to resurrect you and recompense you, ﴿and sends down provision for you from the sky﴾, meaning rain and other things. And despite that clarification and this manifestation, ﴿none takes heed except one who turns back﴾, meaning none is admonished except one whose nature is to turn back to his Lord, the Exalted, in all his affairs.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"So call upon God, making religion sincerely His"﴾ is an address to the monotheists, commanding them, the Exalted, to persist in affirming God's oneness in their worship and to be sincere to God, the Exalted, in all their deeds, even if the disbelievers dislike that, for it does not harm them.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"Exalted in rank, Lord of the Throne"﴾, meaning He is God, Possessor of the lofty ranks and the great Throne. ﴿"He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants"﴾, meaning He casts revelation by His command, which He wills to convey to His creation, upon whomever He wills of His servants, those whom He chooses and informs, so that they may warn His servants of ﴿the Day of Meeting﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, when the people of the earth meet the people of heaven and the created beings meet their Creator. This is His saying: ﴿"that He may warn of the Day of Meeting, the Day when they will come forth"﴾ from their graves, with nothing to conceal them, ﴿"nothing of them is hidden from God"﴾. In this tremendous situation, the Almighty, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿"To whom belongs the dominion today?"﴾ No one answers Him out of awe and fear, so He answers Himself, saying: ﴿"To God, the One, the Subduer. Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned"﴾, good or evil, for the completeness of divine justice. His saying confirms this: ﴿"No injustice today; indeed God is swift in reckoning"﴾, and He begins to call them to account. Before midday has passed, the people of Paradise will be in Paradise, saying in the best resting place. O God, make me one of them, and one who says "Amen."

Guidance from the verses:

1- Apologies are of no use on the Day of Resurrection, even if the servant is permitted to offer an apology; an apology will not benefit him.

2- Affirmation of monotheism and refutation of polytheism and rivalry.

3- Clarification of God's favors upon His servants, as He shows them His signs for their guidance and provides for them while they disbelieve in Him.

4- The obligation to sincerely direct supplication and all other acts of worship to God alone, even if the polytheists dislike that.

5- Affirmation of prophethood, and clarification of its wisdom, which is to warn people of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, when people will be exposed before God with nothing hidden from Him; He will reckon them by His knowledge and justice, so that by the end of the day the people of Paradise will have settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire. O God, protect us from the Fire of Hell.

5- Affirmation of prophethood, and clarification of its wisdom, which is to warn people of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, when people will be exposed before God with nothing hidden from Him; He will reckon them by His knowledge and justice, so that by the end of the day the people of Paradise will have settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire. O God, protect us from the Fire of Hell.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 40, verses 10–17:

Explanation of the words:

﴿ينادون لمقت الله﴾: meaning, the angels call out to them, saying: "God's hatred of you is greater than your hatred of yourselves," and maqt (hatred) is the most intense form of dislike.

﴿إذ تدعون إلى الإيمان فتكفرون﴾: meaning, God's hatred of you when you were in the world and were being called to faith but disbelieved is greater than your hatred of yourselves today, when you have seen the punishment.

﴿أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين﴾: meaning, You caused us to die twice: the first time when we were nonexistent and You created us, and the second time when You caused us to die in the world by taking our souls. And You gave us life twice: the first time when You brought us out of our mothers' wombs alive, and this is one life; and the second time after You raised us from our graves alive.

﴿فاعترفنا بذنوبنا﴾: meaning, our sins, which are denying Your signs and the meeting with You, and associating others with You.

﴿فهل إلى خروج من سبيل﴾: meaning, is there any way back to the life of the world a second time, so that we may believe in You, affirm Your oneness, obey You, and not disobey You?

﴿ذلكم﴾: meaning, the punishment you are in.

﴿بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم﴾: meaning, because when God alone was called upon, you disbelieved in His oneness.

﴿يريكم آياته﴾: meaning, the proofs of His oneness and His power to resurrect you and to recompense you.

﴿وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب﴾: meaning, none takes heed except the one who turns back to God and returns to Him in His oneness.

﴿يلقي الروح من أمره﴾: meaning, He casts revelation by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants.

﴿لينذر يوم التلاق﴾: meaning, so that He may warn, through the one to whom revelation is sent from among mankind, who is the Messenger, of the Day when the people of heaven and the people of earth meet, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿يوم هم بارزون﴾: meaning, nothing shields them, neither mountain, nor tree, nor stone.

﴿لمن الملك اليوم﴾: meaning, to whom belongs the sovereignty today.

Meaning of the verses:

After He mentioned the condition of the believers, that they and their spouses and offspring are in the abode of bliss, in these three verses He describes the condition of the disbelievers in the Fire, following the Qur'an's method of encouragement and warning. He, the Exalted, said, reporting about the people of the Fire: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved﴾, meaning, in their Lord, in meeting Him, and in His oneness, ﴿will be called out to﴾, meaning, the angels will call out to them, saying to them, after they begin to loathe themselves and curse one another: ﴿"The hatred of God is greater than your hatred of yourselves"﴾, because you used to be called to faith in God, His oneness, and obedience, but you disbelieved and rejected it out of arrogance.

Here, in the second verse [11], they will say while in Hell: ﴿"Our Lord"﴾, meaning, O our Lord, ﴿"You have caused us to die twice and You have given us life twice"﴾. By the two deaths they mean: the first, when they were lifeless drops of semen, and the second, the taking of their souls at the end of their terms. By the two lives they mean: the first, which they had in the world before their death, and the second, which is after the resurrection. Their saying ﴿"So we have acknowledged our sins"﴾ means the sins they committed in the worldly life, which are disbelief, polytheism, and disobedience. Their saying after this confession, ﴿"Is there any way out?"﴾, means: is there any path to leave the Fire and return to the worldly life so that we may correct what we corrupted and obey Him whom we disobeyed? The answer is definitely: there is no way to that at all, and your remaining in the punishment is not an injustice to you, but a just recompense for you. Then He mentioned the cause of their punishment in His saying: ﴿"That is because when God alone was called upon, you disbelieved"﴾ in God and His oneness, ﴿"but when partners were associated with Him, you believed"﴾, meaning, when God was associated with others you believed, like your saying "Here I am, no partner have You, except a partner who belongs to You, You possess him and what he possesses," and His saying, "So judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Great." He has decreed your punishment, so there is no path to your salvation.

"So loathe yourselves and lament over your souls; this will neither benefit you nor lighten the punishment for you." His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"It is He who shows you His signs"﴾ is an address to people in this worldly life, an address to the polytheists of Quraysh. After He presented to them a true, living picture of their condition in Hell on the Day of Resurrection, He returned to address them, calling them to faith. He said: He, that is the God who is truly worthy of worship, ﴿who shows you His signs﴾, meaning His proofs and the signs of His oneness and His power to resurrect you and recompense you, ﴿and sends down provision for you from the sky﴾, meaning rain and other things. And despite that clarification and this manifestation, ﴿none takes heed except one who turns back﴾, meaning none is admonished except one whose nature is to turn back to his Lord, the Exalted, in all his affairs.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"So call upon God, making religion sincerely His"﴾ is an address to the monotheists, commanding them, the Exalted, to persist in affirming God's oneness in their worship and to be sincere to God, the Exalted, in all their deeds, even if the disbelievers dislike that, for it does not harm them.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"Exalted in rank, Lord of the Throne"﴾, meaning He is God, Possessor of the lofty ranks and the great Throne. ﴿"He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants"﴾, meaning He casts revelation by His command, which He wills to convey to His creation, upon whomever He wills of His servants, those whom He chooses and informs, so that they may warn His servants of ﴿the Day of Meeting﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, when the people of the earth meet the people of heaven and the created beings meet their Creator. This is His saying: ﴿"that He may warn of the Day of Meeting, the Day when they will come forth"﴾ from their graves, with nothing to conceal them, ﴿"nothing of them is hidden from God"﴾. In this tremendous situation, the Almighty, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿"To whom belongs the dominion today?"﴾ No one answers Him out of awe and fear, so He answers Himself, saying: ﴿"To God, the One, the Subduer. Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned"﴾, good or evil, for the completeness of divine justice. His saying confirms this: ﴿"No injustice today; indeed God is swift in reckoning"﴾, and He begins to call them to account. Before midday has passed, the people of Paradise will be in Paradise, saying in the best resting place. O God, make me one of them, and one who says "Amen."

Guidance from the verses:

1- Apologies are of no use on the Day of Resurrection, even if the servant is permitted to offer an apology; an apology will not benefit him.

2- Affirmation of monotheism and refutation of polytheism and rivalry.

3- Clarification of God's favors upon His servants, as He shows them His signs for their guidance and provides for them while they disbelieve in Him.

4- The obligation to sincerely direct supplication and all other acts of worship to God alone, even if the polytheists dislike that.

5- Affirmation of prophethood, and clarification of its wisdom, which is to warn people of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, when people will be exposed before God with nothing hidden from Him; He will reckon them by His knowledge and justice, so that by the end of the day the people of Paradise will have settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire. O God, protect us from the Fire of Hell.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 40, verses 18–20:

Explanation of the words:

Yawm al-Azifah (the Imminent Day): that is, the Day of Resurrection.

Idh al-qulubu ladayl-hanajir (when the hearts rise up to the throats): that is, from the intensity of fear the hearts will have risen until they reach the throats.

Kazimin (suppressing): that is, they wish to return their hearts to their places but are unable to.

Ma lilzalimina min hamim (the wrongdoers will have no intimate friend): that is, the polytheists will have no loving friend, whether near or far.

Ya'lamu khaa'innat al-a'yun (He knows the treachery of the eyes): that is, God Most High knows the eye when it steals a glance at what is forbidden.

Wallahu yaqdi bil-haqq (God judges with truth): that is, by the perfection of His power and knowledge He judges with truth.

Wal-ladhina yad'una min dunihi (and those whom they call upon besides Him): that is, the idols which the polytheists of Quraysh invoke do not judge anything, whether justly or unjustly, because they are idols that neither hear nor see.

Meaning of the verses:

After explaining the difficult situation on the plains of Resurrection in the preceding verses, God Most High said to His Messenger: ﴿And warn them﴾, O Our Messenger, that is, warn your people, ﴿of the Imminent Day﴾, which is the near Resurrection that has in fact drawn near, and everything that is coming is near. Warn them of its nearness so that they do not meet it with polytheism and sins, and so that they do not suffer a manifest loss. Warn them of the Imminent Day, when the hearts, from the intensity of fear, rise up to the throats while they suppress them, so that they neither come out and they die, nor return to their places and they rest. ﴿There will be no intimate friend for the wrongdoers﴾, who are the people of polytheism and sins, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ whose intercession is accepted and obeyed on their behalf. Neither this nor that; how terrible the condition!

As for His saying: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes﴾, He informs of the vastness of His knowledge and the comprehensiveness of His awareness, that He knows the treachery of the eyes, which is the eye stealing glances at what is forbidden. And He knows ﴿what the breasts conceal﴾, that is, what the hearts of the servants hide and harbor of good and evil. Therefore the reckoning will be precise, and whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning will be punished. ﴿And God judges with truth﴾, that is, He judges with justice. ﴿And those whom they call upon besides Him﴾, that is, those whom the polytheists worship of idols and images, ﴿do not judge anything﴾, because they neither hear nor see.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾: He hears the words of His servants and sees their deeds and conditions. Therefore, when He judges, He judges with truth, and He is able to enforce the judgment, so He recompenses an evil deed with its like and a good deed with ten times its like.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the terror of the Day of Resurrection and the difficulty of the standing there.

2- The absence of an intimate friend and an intercessor for the wrongdoers on the Day of Resurrection.

3- Explanation of the vastness of God's knowledge, to the extent that He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.

4- God's judgment is just, and His decree is binding, because of the perfection of His knowledge and power.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 40, verse 21–22:

Explanation of the words:

Aw lam yasiru fi al-ardi (Did they not travel through the land?): That is, the disbelievers of Quraysh neglected and did not travel through the land.

Fa-yanzuru (and see): That is, with their own eyes.

Kayfa kana 'aqibatu alladhina kanu min qablihim (how was the end of those who were before them): It was destruction, loss and ruin upon them.

Kanu hum ashadda minhum quwwatan wa athaaran fi al-ardi (they were stronger than them in power and in traces left upon the earth): And that did not avail them anything from God.

Fa-akhadhahumu Allahu bi-dhunubihim (So God seized them for their sins): That is, He punished them for their sins, so He destroyed and annihilated them.

Wa ma kana lahum mina Allahi min waqin (and they had no protector from God): That is, no protection from the punishment of God was found for them that could shield them from it.

Dhalika bi-annahum kanat ta'tihim rusuluhum bi-al-bayyinat (That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs): That is, with arguments, demonstrations, evidences and miracles.

Fa-kafaru (so they disbelieved): That is, in those proofs and signs.

Fa-akhadhahumu Allah (so God seized them): That is, when they disbelieved, He seized them for their disbelief.

Innahu qawiyyun shadidu al-'iqab (Indeed He is Strong, Severe in punishment): This is the reason given for His seizing them.

Meaning of the verses:

The context has already conveyed God's warning to the polytheists of Quraysh of the punishment of the Hereafter, and, in an effort to advise them and seek their guidance, He frightened them, after the punishment of the Hereafter, with the punishment of this world, so that perhaps they would repent. He said: "Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those who came before them? They were stronger than them and left more traces upon the earth." That is, these stubborn deniers neglected and did not travel through the lands, northward and southward, where the dwellings of 'Ad lie in the south and the dwellings of Thamud in the north, so that they might see with their own eyes how was the end of those before them, such as 'Ad and Thamud. Those were stronger than these in power and traces upon the earth in terms of building, prosperity, and capacity for war and fighting. "So God seized them for their sins," that is, for the sins of polytheism, denial and disobedience. When He seized them, there was no protector from God's punishment and torment to shield them from what God sent down upon them and what He brought down upon their courtyards. So what is the matter with these polytheists that they do not take heed and do not learn a lesson? The wise one is he who learns from others.

His saying, exalted is He: "That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so God seized them." This is the reason for God's seizing of those peoples, such as 'Ad, Thamud and others, since He seized them only after He had warned them and given them excuse. When they persisted in disbelief and denial, He seized them for their sins. And His saying, "Indeed He is Strong, Severe in punishment," is also a reason for the complete seizure with which He seized them, because of the greatness of His power and the severity of His punishment.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of the saying: The wise one is he who learns from others.

2- Seizing for sins is a sunnah (established way) of God in the earth that does not change or alter.

3- Whoever God wills to punish, there is no protector who can shield him, nor any defender who can protect him; and whoever repents, God turns to him in forgiveness.

**Explanation of the words:**

**"With Our signs and a clear authority"**: That is, with Our proofs and an evident, manifest demonstration.

**"Haman and Qarun"**: Haman was the minister of Pharaoh (Fir'awn), and Qarun was a man of great wealth.

**"They said: a sorcerer, a liar"**: That is, when they saw the sign of the staff and the white hand, they said, "A sorcerer, a liar," to repel their people so that they would not believe in him.

**"When he came to them with the truth from Us"**: That is, when Moses came to them with the truth regarding what he told them, that he was a Messenger of God, and demanded that they send the Children of Israel with him.

**"They said: Kill the sons of those who believed with him"**: That is, kill the male children.

**"And spare their women"**: That is, their daughters, meaning let them live.

**"And the scheming of the disbelievers is only in error"**: That is, their plotting is only in loss and perdition.

**"Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord"**: That is, let me be, leave me alone, and let him call upon his Lord to protect him from me.

**"Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion"**: That is, he will alter your worship of your gods into worship of his God.

**"Or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land"**: Through killing, destruction, and the like.

**"Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord"**: That is, I have sought protection with my Creator and your Creator.

**"From every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning"**: That is, from every arrogant person who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning and recompense for deeds.

**Meaning of the verses:**

After that divine call to the Quraysh to faith, monotheism, and belief in the Resurrection and recompense, and after the manifestations of God's power, knowledge, wisdom, and justice contained in it, and after that presentation of the conditions of the Resurrection and the explanation of the recompense for both disbelievers and believers therein, as if it were seen with the eye, and after that encouragement and warning concerning this world and the Hereafter, while the polytheists only increase in obstinacy and transgression, God Most High recounted to His Messenger the story of Moses with Pharaoh, to console him and make him patient, and to inform him that affliction, however severe, is followed by relief, and that God will support him against his people just as He supported Moses against Pharaoh and his people. So He, Exalted, said: **"And We certainly sent Moses, son of Imran, with Our signs"**, that is, before you, O Our Messenger, with Our proofs and evidences of the truthfulness of his call and the soundness of his mission, **"and a clear authority"**, that is, and a manifest, evident demonstration, We sent him to Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun. Haman was Pharaoh's minister, and Qarun was one of the lords of wealth. Although he was not of Pharaoh's family, since he was of the Children of Israel, he sided with Pharaoh and stood in his camp. When Moses conveyed to them his Lord's call and showed them the proofs and demonstrations, they said, "A sorcerer, a liar." Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 40, verse 28–29:

Explanation of the words:

"And a man from the family of Pharaoh said": he was Shim'an, the paternal cousin of Pharaoh.

"Will you kill a man because he says, 'My Lord is Allah'?": i.e., merely because he says, "My Lord is Allah." The man is Musa (peace be upon him).

"With clear proofs from your Lord": i.e., with manifest miracles.

"Then his lie will be upon himself": i.e., the harm of his lie falls upon him, not upon you.

"Some of what he threatens you with will befall you": i.e., some of the punishment he threatens you with in this world, swiftly and not later.

"Surely Allah does not guide one who is an extravagant liar": i.e., one who is extravagant in disbelief and wrongdoing, a liar who does not speak the truth nor utter it.

"Dominant in the land": i.e., prevailing in the lands of Egypt and its territories.

"Who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes upon us?": i.e., against the punishment of Allah if it comes upon us, since we have killed His friends.

"I show you only what I see": i.e., I advise you only with what I advise myself, and that is killing Musa.

"And I guide you only to the path of right conduct": i.e., only to the way of rectitude and correctness.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with what took place in Pharaoh's palace. Pharaoh expressed his desire to execute Musa, justifying this by two matters: that he would change the religion of the state and the people, and that he would spread turmoil in the land and fatigue to the state and the citizens alike. Here is a believing man from the men of the palace, concealing his faith in Musa and in the monotheism he brought, out of fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs. Let us listen to what Allah, the Exalted, tells us about him: ﴿And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh said﴾, meaning, a believer in Musa, ﴿from the family of Pharaoh﴾, for he was a paternal cousin of Pharaoh, named Shim'an, like Salman. He said: ﴿Will you kill a man because he says, "My Lord is Allah"?﴾ He denounces their decision to kill, ﴿because he says, "My Lord is Allah"﴾, i.e., because he said, "My Lord is Allah," ﴿and he has certainly brought you clear proofs from your Lord﴾, which are the arguments and demonstrations such as the staff and the hand, ﴿from your Lord﴾, the Truth, to whom there is no lord for you besides Him. ﴿And if he is a liar﴾, meaning, even if we suppose he is a liar, the harm of his lie returns upon him, not upon you. ﴿And if he is truthful﴾, and he is truthful, ﴿some of what he threatens you with will befall you﴾, of the swift punishment. Indeed, Allah does not guide, i.e., does not grant success, to victory and triumph in his affairs, ﴿one who is an extravagant liar﴾, one who exceeds the limit in transgression and wrongdoing, ﴿a liar﴾, a fabricator who lives on lies and so does not know truth. After he had shown them this established scientific truth, he turned to them admonishing them, saying: ﴿O my people, the kingdom is yours today, dominant in the land﴾, meaning, prevailing in the land, the land of Egypt in its entire soil and boundaries. But if we exceed the limit in wrongdoing and fabrication, killing the friends of Allah, the might of Allah will come upon us as punishment, so who will help us? Indeed, there is no helper for us ever from Allah. So understand well what I have told you. "No one is destroyed before Allah except the destroyed." Here Pharaoh rose to respond to the words of the believing man, and he said what Allah, the Exalted, reported of him in His saying: ﴿Pharaoh said, "I show you only what I see"﴾, meaning, I advise you of nothing except what I have seen to be correct and sound, namely the killing of Musa, peace be upon him, ﴿and I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾, i.e., only to the way of truth and correctness. And he lied, by Allah.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The virtue of faith and the virtue of its possessor: praise is recorded for this man alongside three men, namely the believer of the family of Pharaoh here, Habib the carpenter, the believer of the family of Yasin, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

2- The eloquence of the believer of the family of Pharaoh is the fruit of his faith and its swift blessing, for his words had a great effect on hearts.

3- Condemnation of extravagance in everything, and of lying and fabrication in everything and about anything.

4- Among the strange matters concerning Pharaoh is his claim to guide to rectitude, soundness and correctness in speech and action, to the extent that he became a proverb, and it was said: "Pharaoh guides to rectitude."

2- The eloquence of the believer of the family of Pharaoh is the fruit of his faith and its swift blessing, for his words had a great effect on hearts.

3- Condemnation of extravagance in everything, and of lying and fabrication in everything and about anything.

4- Among the strange matters concerning Pharaoh is his claim to guide to rectitude, soundness and correctness in speech and action, to the extent that he became a proverb, and it was said: "Pharaoh guides to rectitude."

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with what was discussed in the council of the government. After this eloquent admonition he said: ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾, indicating that the people had not been moved by his words. So he consoled himself, relying on his knowledge of Allah's disposition in His creation, and said: ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾. Whoever Allah has decreed misguidance for will reach wretchedness through his own acquisition, so he has no guide ever, since Allah does not guide one whom He has led astray. Then he said to them, continuing his speech: ﴿And Joseph had certainly come to you before﴾, that is, before Moses, namely Joseph son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, peace be upon them, with clear evidences and proofs indicating the oneness of Allah and the obligation of obeying Him. Then he informed them that those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah intend to nullify the truth and extinguish its light with their words, with no proof or demonstration in their possession. Here the words of the believing man end, and the speech now turns to the tyrant Pharaoh, which we will read in the following verses after seeing the guidance contained in these verses.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 40, verses 36–40:

Explanation of the words:

﴿يا هامان ابن لي صرحا﴾ "O Haman, build me a lofty structure" (ṣarḥ): Haman was the minister of Pharaoh, and ṣarḥ means a high building.

أسباب السماوات (asbāb al-samāwāt): that is, its paths that lead to them.

﴿وإني لأظنه كاذباً﴾ "And indeed I think him a liar": that is, I think Moses is lying in his claim that he has a god other than me.

﴿سوء علمه﴾ (sū' 'amalihi): that is, the ugliness of his deed.

﴿وصد عن السبيل﴾ "and he was barred from the way": that is, from the path of guidance.

﴿إلا في تباب﴾ "except in ruin": that is, loss and perdition with no benefit worth mentioning.

﴿إنما هذه الحياة الدنيا متاع﴾ "Indeed, this worldly life is but a passing enjoyment": that is, this world is nothing but a enjoyment one takes for a time, and then it vanishes.

﴿دار القرار﴾ (dār al-qarār): that is, the place of settlement and everlasting abiding.

﴿يرزقون فيها بغير حساب﴾ "they will be provided for therein without reckoning": that is, abundant provision without any accountability or consequence.

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with what passes between the believing man of Pharaoh's people and Pharaoh himself, since the believer's words, with their advice and guidance, have already been mentioned. Here Pharaoh responds, indirectly, to what the believer said. He said to his minister Haman: ﴿O Haman, build me a lofty structure﴾, that is, a high building, ﴿that I may reach the means, the means of the heavens, and look upon the god of Moses; and indeed I think him a liar﴾, that is, in his claim that he has a god other than me. This is from Pharaoh merely a deceitful maneuver, by which he wishes to deceive others in order to preserve his position. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾, that is, a similar embellishment in Pharaoh's words made the worst of his deeds seem appealing to him, ﴿and he was barred from the way﴾, that is, he was turned away from the path of truth and guidance. And His saying: ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin﴾, that is, his scheming and planning to kill Moses, peace be upon him, and to kill the sons of the believers, ﴿except in ruin﴾, that is, loss and perdition, in which nothing of it was realized, because God, may He be exalted, is the protector of Moses and the believers, so Pharaoh was never able to prevail over them in any way.

After informing us about Pharaoh and his failed attempt, God, may He be exalted, informed us about the believing man and what he said to the people of counsel and guidance, saying: ﴿And the one who believed said: O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct﴾, that is, the path of rectitude and correctness in your lives, so that you may be saved from punishment and attain the lasting bliss of Paradise. He said: ﴿O my people, indeed this worldly life is but a passing enjoyment﴾, that is, it is nothing more than a little enjoyment that is used for a time and then goes away quickly. ﴿And indeed the Hereafter﴾, that is, the life to come after this life ends, ﴿is the abode of settlement﴾, that is, the place of stability and everlasting residence. So work for the abode of permanence and turn away from the abode of impermanence, and know that the reckoning is swift, and that ﴿whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its equivalent﴾, and that is due to the justice of the Lord, blessed and exalted. And whoever does a righteous deed, from among the righteous deeds that God has legislated for His servants and made them worship through, while being a believer, that is, one who affirms God and His promise and threat on the Day of meeting Him, then those, that is, the believers who do righteous deeds, whether male or female, will enter Paradise, the abode of peace, and they will be provided for therein without reckoning, that is, abundant provision that does not bring its possessor any consequence, weariness, or fatigue.

Lessons from the verses:

1. A warning against the adornment of evil deeds, which results from becoming accustomed to them and persisting in doing them; whoever has his evil deeds made attractive to him, so that he comes to see them as good, is ruined, and we seek refuge in God.

2. A warning against being deceived by this world and heedless of the Hereafter, since the first is passing and the second is lasting, and preferring the lasting over the transient is the way of the wise.

3. The legitimacy of reminding people of the reckoning and of the recompense, and of the happiness and misery that take place in the Hereafter.

﴿إنما هذه الحياة الدنيا متاع﴾ "Indeed, this worldly life is but a passing enjoyment": that is, this world is nothing but a enjoyment one takes for a time, and then it vanishes.

﴿دار القرار﴾ (dār al-qarār): that is, the place of settlement and everlasting abiding.

﴿يرزقون فيها بغير حساب﴾ "they will be provided for therein without reckoning": that is, abundant provision without any accountability or consequence.

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with what passes between the believing man of Pharaoh's people and Pharaoh himself, since the believer's words, with their advice and guidance, have already been mentioned. Here Pharaoh responds, indirectly, to what the believer said. He said to his minister Haman: ﴿O Haman, build me a lofty structure﴾, that is, a high building, ﴿that I may reach the means, the means of the heavens, and look upon the god of Moses; and indeed I think him a liar﴾, that is, in his claim that he has a god other than me. This is from Pharaoh merely a deceitful maneuver, by which he wishes to deceive others in order to preserve his position. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾, that is, a similar embellishment in Pharaoh's words made the worst of his deeds seem appealing to him, ﴿and he was barred from the way﴾, that is, he was turned away from the path of truth and guidance. And His saying: ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin﴾, that is, his scheming and planning to kill Moses, peace be upon him, and to kill the sons of the believers, ﴿except in ruin﴾, that is, loss and perdition, in which nothing of it was realized, because God, may He be exalted, is the protector of Moses and the believers, so Pharaoh was never able to prevail over them in any way.

After informing us about Pharaoh and his failed attempt, God, may He be exalted, informed us about the believing man and what he said to the people of counsel and guidance, saying: ﴿And the one who believed said: O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct﴾, that is, the path of rectitude and correctness in your lives, so that you may be saved from punishment and attain the lasting bliss of Paradise. He said: ﴿O my people, indeed this worldly life is but a passing enjoyment﴾, that is, it is nothing more than a little enjoyment that is used for a time and then goes away quickly. ﴿And indeed the Hereafter﴾, that is, the life to come after this life ends, ﴿is the abode of settlement﴾, that is, the place of stability and everlasting residence. So work for the abode of permanence and turn away from the abode of impermanence, and know that the reckoning is swift, and that ﴿whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its equivalent﴾, and that is due to the justice of the Lord, blessed and exalted. And whoever does a righteous deed, from among the righteous deeds that God has legislated for His servants and made them worship through, while being a believer, that is, one who affirms God and His promise and threat on the Day of meeting Him, then those, that is, the believers who do righteous deeds, whether male or female, will enter Paradise, the abode of peace, and they will be provided for therein without reckoning, that is, abundant provision that does not bring its possessor any consequence, weariness, or fatigue.

Lessons from the verses:

1. A warning against the adornment of evil deeds, which results from becoming accustomed to them and persisting in doing them; whoever has his evil deeds made attractive to him, so that he comes to see them as good, is ruined, and we seek refuge in God.

2. A warning against being deceived by this world and heedless of the Hereafter, since the first is passing and the second is lasting, and preferring the lasting over the transient is the way of the wise.

3. The legitimacy of reminding people of the reckoning and of the recompense, and of the happiness and misery that take place in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 40, verses 41–46:

Explanation of the words:

"Adu'ukum ila al-najah" (I call you to salvation): that is, to be saved from loss in this world and the Hereafter, by means of faith and righteous deeds.

"Wa tad'unani ila al-nar" (and you call me to the Fire): that is, to the punishment of the Fire, by means of disbelief and associating partners with Allah, exalted is He.

"Ma laysa li bihi 'ilm" (of which I have no knowledge): that is, I have no knowledge of the validity of His being associated in the worship of Allah, exalted is He.

"Wa ana ad'ukum ila al-'Aziz al-Ghaffar" (while I call you to the Almighty, the Ever-Forgiving): that is, while I call you to faith and to the worship of Allah, the Almighty, that is, the One who prevails over His affair, the Ever-Forgiving to the sins of the repentant among the believing worshippers of Him.

"La jarama anna ma tad'unani ilayhi" (Truly, that to which you call me): that is, truly, that to which you call me to believe in and worship.

"Laysa lahu da'watun fi al-dunya wa al-akhirah" (has no call [answered] in this world or the Hereafter): that is, there is no true call to His worship for it, and no call of response, in that it would answer one who calls upon it, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

"Wa anna al-musrifina hum ashab al-nar" (and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire): that is, and that the transgressors in disbelief, polytheism and sins are the people of the Fire, which is obligatory for them.

"Fawaqahu Allah sayyi'at ma makaru" (So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted): that is, Allah preserved him from their scheme against him to kill him.

"Wa haqa bi-al Fir'awn su' al-'adhab" (And there befell the people of Pharaoh the worst of punishment): that is, the punishment of drowning, when Pharaoh and all his soldiers were drowned.

"Al-nar yu'radun 'alayha ghuduwwan wa 'ashiyyan" (The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening): that is, the worst punishment is the Fire, to which they are exposed morning and evening, because their souls are in the crops of black birds, which are presented to the Fire twice each day.

"Wa yawm al-qiyamah adkhilu al-Fir'awn" (And on the Day of Resurrection: "Admit the people of Pharaoh"): that is, and on the Day of Resurrection it will be said: "Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment."

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the advice and guidance of the believer from the family of Pharaoh, as he said what Allah related about him in His words: "O my people, how is it that I call you to salvation" — that is, from the Fire, by means of faith and righteous deeds, together with abandoning polytheism and sins — "while you call me to the Fire," by your calling me to polytheism and disbelief, you call me to disbelieve in Allah and associate others with Him, "of which I have no knowledge," that is, of which I have no knowledge of the validity of His being associated in the worship of Allah, exalted is He. "And I call you to the Almighty, the Ever-Forgiving," that is, so that you may believe in Him, worship Him alone, and not associate anything with Him. "I call you to the Almighty," that is, the One who prevails and cannot be overcome, "the Ever-Forgiving" to the sins of the repentant among His servants, whatever their gravity; "and you call me to that which is the most abased and worthless thing, which neither benefits nor harms, for it neither hears nor sees." "Truly," that is, certainly, "that to which you call me, to believe in it and worship it, has no true call by which it may be invoked, nor any call of response, for it will never answer me in prayer, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter." And another matter, O my people: "our return is to Allah," that is, we will certainly return to Him, so it is obligatory that we believe in Him, worship Him and make Him alone our God, for as long as our return is to Him. And another: "and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire," the transgressors who exceed the limit in disbelief, polytheism and sins, they are the companions of the Fire, that is, its people, who will never leave it and it will never leave them.

His words: "So you will remember what I say to you" appear to have been said when they rejected his call and resolved to kill him, and this is indicated by his saying: "And I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants."

His exalted words: "So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted" — that is, Allah preserved him from their scheme against him to kill him, so Allah saved him when he fled from them. Pharaoh then sent men in pursuit of him, but they could not reach him, and he was saved along with Moses and the Children of Israel. His words: "And there befell the people of Pharaoh the worst of punishment," which was that Allah drowned them all in the sea.

His words: "The Fire, they are exposed to it" are a report that the souls of the people of Pharaoh are exposed in the barzakh to the Fire morning and evening, because they are in the crops of black birds, unlike the souls of the believers, which are in the crops of green birds that graze in Paradise, until the Day of Resurrection.

"And on the day the Hour is established, it will be said: Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment," which is the punishment of Hell, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of the great difference between one who calls to salvation and one who calls to the Fire, between one who calls to the Almighty, the Ever-Forgiving, that He may be believed in and worshipped, and one who calls to idols that neither hear nor see and are the most abject and worthless thing in life, and between one who calls upon one who does not respond in this world or the Hereafter and one who calls upon one who responds in this world and the Hereafter.

2- Condemnation of extravagance (israf) in everything.

3- How excellent is what the believer of the family of Pharaoh concluded his admonition and counsel to his people with: "So you will remember what I say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants."

4- Affirmation of the punishment of the grave and its bliss, since the souls of the family of Pharaoh are exposed to the Fire morning and evening.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 40, verses 47–52:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And when they dispute with one another in the Fire﴾: That is, warn them of the Day of the Imminent (al-Azifa), and when they dispute with one another in the Fire, i.e., they argue.

﴿Then the weak will say﴾: That is, the weak followers who followed the rich and the powerful in polytheism.

﴿Indeed, we were to you followers﴾: That is, following you in what you believed and did.

﴿So will you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?﴾: That is, will you avert from us any part of the Fire?

﴿Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants﴾: So there is no further appeal ever. He has judged for the people of faith and piety to Paradise, so they are in Paradise, and for the people of polytheism and sin to the Fire, so they are in the Fire.

﴿To the keepers of Hell﴾: That is, the plural of khazin (keeper), the one entrusted with the Fire and its people.

﴿Lighten for us a day of the punishment﴾: That is, an amount equal to one day of the days of this world, since the Hereafter is one day without a night.

﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world﴾: That is, by making their religion prevail, or by destroying their people and saving them from destruction.

﴿And the day when the witnesses will stand﴾: That is, and He will support them on the day when the witnesses stand, and they are the angels who testify for the messengers that they conveyed the message.

﴿And for them is the curse, and for them is the worst abode﴾: That is, for them is the curse, i.e., distance from mercy; and for them is the worst abode, i.e., the Hereafter, meaning the severity of its punishment.

Explanation of the verses:

This is another presentation of the Fire and what takes place in it, after the presentation concerning the people of Pharaoh in the Fire. It is presented to the disbelievers of Quraysh so that they may witness their destiny through it if they do not repent to Allah from disbelief, denial and polytheism. It is contained in six verses. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And [mention] when they dispute with one another in the Fire﴾, i.e., warn them and remind them of when they argue with one another in it. The weak, the followers who used to follow the wealthy and powerful of the land out of greed for them and fear of them, will say to those who were arrogant with their strength against faith and following the messengers: ﴿Indeed, we were to you followers﴾, i.e., following you. ﴿So will you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?﴾, i.e., is it within your ability to lighten for us some share of the punishment of the Fire? They answered them, saying what Allah the Exalted related about them in His saying: ﴿Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, all of us are within it"﴾, i.e., we and you. "Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants," having decreed Paradise for the people of faith and piety, and the Fire for the people of polytheism and sin. This was the dispute of the followers with the leaders, and it led to nothing except increased regret, grief and distress. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell﴾, meaning the angels charged with the Fire and its punishment, they will say to them: ﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment﴾, i.e., an amount equal to one day of the days of this world, since in the Hereafter there is no night; rather it is one day. The angels responded to them, saying what Allah the Exalted related about them in His saying: ﴿They said, "Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?"﴾, i.e., do you say, "Call upon your Lord to lighten the punishment for you," when there did not come to you your messengers with the clear proofs indicating the obligation of faith and piety through abandoning polytheism and sins? They said, "Yes," i.e., they acknowledged. The angels then said to them: "Then call upon [Him] yourselves. But the supplication of the disbelievers is not but in error," so it will never be answered.

And His saying the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers﴾ is an affirmation of a great truth, which is that it is among the way of Allah with His messengers that He supports them by making their religion prevail and what they guide to and call to, even if time is prolonged and trials and tribulations intensify; or by destroying their disbelieving peoples and saving them and the believers with them. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world﴾. And His saying: ﴿And the day when the witnesses will stand﴾, i.e., and He will support them in the Hereafter on the day when the witnesses stand, and they are the angels who testify for the messengers that they conveyed, and against the disbelievers for their denial.

And His saying: ﴿The day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾, meaning, if they are permitted to offer excuses, their excuses will not be accepted. ﴿And for them is the curse﴾, i.e., distance from mercy and Paradise. ﴿And for them is the worst abode﴾, the Hereafter, and it is the severest of its punishment.

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1. Clarification of the dispute of the people of the Fire, which is the argument that takes place between the followers and the leaders.

2. Condemnation of pride and arrogance, for pride is an obstacle to obedience and steadfastness.

3. The supplication of the disbeliever is not answered in this world or the Hereafter, except as Allah wills.

4. Excuses are not accepted on the Day of Resurrection.

5. Supplication is not answered in the Fire.

6. Clarification of Allah's promise to His messengers and the believers, that He will support them in one of two ways: first, by making their religion victorious, establishing and affirming it even if time is prolonged; and second, by destroying their enemy and saving them.
